acip: ,LAS DE BYAS PA'I SKAD CIG GNYIS PAR ZHIG NA NI, MTSAMS DE NAS 'BRAS BU DNGOS SU 'BYIN PA'I SNGA LOGS KYI BAR DU LAS DE MED LA, LAS ZHIG PA YANG DNGOS POR MED PAS LAS LAS 'BRAS BU JI LTAR 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR ZHES BRTZAD PA'I LAN DU,
wylie: las de byas pa'i skad cig gnyis par zhig na ni, mtshams de nas 'bras bu dngos su 'byin pa'i snga logs kyi bar du las de med la, las zhig pa yang dngos por med pas las las 'bras bu ji ltar 'byung bar 'gyur zhes brtsad pa'i lan du
english: From the moment after you complete a karma or deed, that deed is finished and gone. During the entire period from that point up to the point at which the consequence actually occurs, the deed no longer exists. A deed which is already gone is no longer a thing that can have any affect on anything. How then does a deed or karma ever produce any kind of consequence? Here is how we explain this problem:

acip: ,DE RNAMS KYI DON NI SNGAR BZHIN BRTZAD PA'I LAN SMRA BA PO BZHI GAS KYANG , LAS LA SKYE BA DANG 'GAG PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHAS LEN ZHING , LAS BYAS PA'I 'OG TU 'GAGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DOD DO, , DE LA SLOB DPON 'DIS DE 'DRA BA'I 'GAGS PA YIN KYANG KUN GZHI SOGS KHAS LEN PAS SKYON MED CES LAN 'DEBS PA MI RIGS TE, RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA'I TSUL GYIS LAS SKYE BA DANG 'GAGS PA MED PA'I PHYIR RO ZHES 'GOG PA YIN NO,
wylie: de rnams kyi don ni sngar bzhin brtsad pa'i lan smra ba po bzhi gas kyang , las la skye ba dang 'gag pa rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa khas len zhing , las byas pa'i 'og tu 'gags pa de rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dod do, , de la slob dpon 'dis de 'dra ba'i 'gags pa yin kyang kun gzhi sogs khas len pas skyon med ces lan 'debs pa mi rigs te, rang bzhin gyis grub pa'i tshul gyis las skye ba dang 'gags pa med pa'i phyir ro zhes 'gog pa yin no
english: The point of all this is that all four of the positions above, as they attempt to answer the problem raised, do so from a viewpoint of accepting that a deed has a beginning that exists by definition and an ending too that exists by definition. They are agreeing as well that the later condition of the deed's having ended is something that exists by definition. The Master [Chandrakirti] is stating that it is improper to answer the problem raised above by saying that, "Even though the ending of the deed is that way, it's no problem, because we believe in foundation consciousness." He is denying all these positions, for the reason that there simply doesn't even exist any beginning or ending of a deed that could occur through any nature of its own.

acip: ,PHUG GAM LHA KHANG STONG PA'AM, ,LJON SHING DRUNG DU GNAS BCAS TE, ,NAM ZHIG RGYAB TU MI LTA ZHING , ,CHAGS PA MED PAR 'GYUR ZHIG GU,
wylie: phug gam lha khang stong pa'am, ,ljon shing drung du gnas bcas te, ,nam zhig rgyab tu mi lta zhing , ,chags pa med par 'gyur zhig gu
english: May I come to live in a cave somewhere, Or in some abandoned temple, or else At the foot of a forest tree. May the day never come that I look back At all, may I reach a place Where I've finished with every attachment.

acip: ,GNYIS PA NI, GNAS BRAG DANG SA'I PHUG GAM LHA KHANG STONG PA'AM LJON SHING GI DRUNG DU JI SRID 'DOD PAR GNAS BCAS TE KHYIM LA SOGS PA SNGAR SPANGS PA DE DAG PHYIR LEN PAR MI 'DOD PAS NA NAM ZHIG RGYAB TU MI BLTA ZHING , DE DAG LA CHAGS PA MED PAR NAM ZHIG 'GYUR ZHIG GU SNYAM DU SMON PAR BYA'O,
wylie: gnyis pa ni, gnas brag dang sa'i phug gam lha khang stong pa'am ljon shing gi drung du ji srid 'dod par gnas bcas te khyim la sogs pa sngar spangs pa de dag phyir len par mi 'dod pas na nam zhig rgyab tu mi blta zhing , de dag la chags pa med par nam zhig 'gyur zhig gu snyam du smon par bya'o
english: Here is the second point, on where I should go into isolation. Make to yourself the following prayer as well: "May I come to live exactly as I please, in a cave somewhere, or in some hollow, or perhaps in some abandoned temple, or else at the foot of a forest tree. May the day never come that I look back at all, when I think of the home and other things that I used to have and then gave up; may I never get any wish at all to have them back. May I reach, in short, a place where I've finished with every kind of attachment for any of these things."

acip: ,GANG ZHIG KUN LA LTOS MED PA, ,DE YI PHUN TSOGS ZAD MI SHES, ,DE BAS LUS KYI 'DOD PA NI, ,'PHEL PHYIR SKABS DBYE MI BYA STE, ,GANG ZHIG YID 'ONG MI 'DZIN PA, ,DE NI DNGOS PO BZANG PO YIN,
wylie: gang zhig kun la ltos med pa, ,de yi phun tshogs zad mi shes, ,de bas lus kyi 'dod pa ni, ,'phel phyir skabs dbye mi bya ste, ,gang zhig yid 'ong mi 'dzin pa, ,de ni dngos po bzang po yin
english: The excellent things that come to those Who depend on nothing at all Are absolutely endless; On the other hand is desire for The body, which grows forever, Leaving you no other chance. He who is finished grasping to Attractions has found the finest Thing to possess of all.

acip: ,DE BAS NA LUS KYI DON DU LONGS SPYOD LA SRED PA'I 'DOD PA NI GNYEN PO MA BSTEN NA GONG NAS GONG DU 'PHEL BAR 'GYUR BA'I PHYIR 'DOD YON LA SRED PAS SKABS DBYE BAR MI BYA STE, GANG ZHIG YID CHAGS PAR 'GYUR BA'I DNGOS PO YID 'ONG MI 'DZIN PA DE NI NOR RNAMS KYI MCHOG TU GYUR PA DNGOS PO BZANG PO YIN NO,
wylie: de bas na lus kyi don du longs spyod la sred pa'i 'dod pa ni gnyen po ma bsten na gong nas gong du 'phel bar 'gyur ba'i phyir 'dod yon la sred pas skabs dbye bar mi bya ste, gang zhig yid chags par 'gyur ba'i dngos po yid 'ong mi 'dzin pa de ni nor rnams kyi mchog tu gyur pa dngos po bzang po yin no
english: On the other hand is the desire where you crave material possessions for the sake of the body; if you fail to apply the antidotes for this attitude, then it grows forever--so that the craving for objects of the senses leaves you with no other chance in your life. He who is finished grasping to things which are attractions, he who has stopped holding them to be attractive, has found the finest thing to possess of all. Contemplation Forty-One The suffering of deciding what is "me"

acip: 'DIR PHYOGS SNGA MA SMRA BAS, BYANG SEMS RNAMS RGYAL BA'I SRAS YIN PAS, BYANG SEMS RGYAL BA LAS 'KHRUNGS PA RIGS KYI, DE LAS BZLOG NAS SMRA BA MI RIGS ZHES BRTZAD PA LA,
wylie: 'dir phyogs snga ma smra bas, byang sems rnams rgyal ba'i sras yin pas, byang sems rgyal ba las 'khrungs pa rigs kyi, de las bzlog nas smra ba mi rigs zhes brtsad pa la
english: At this point, a person who had raised the original issue might persist, expressing the following thought: An argument has been raised which says that—since bodhisattvas are the “sons & daughters” of the victorious Buddhas—it makes sense to say that bodhisattvas are born from the Victorious Ones; but that asserting the reverse does not.

acip: DE'I PHYIR LAM DES NYAN THOS SDE PA GNYIS DANG THUN MONG BA'I NYON MONGS SU BZHAG PA RNAMS, SNGAR BSHAD PA LTAR GYI LAM RGYUD LA BSKYED PAS, RE ZHIG MNGON GYUR DU RGYU BA MED PA'I TSE, NYON MONGS ZAD PA'I GROL BA THOB PAR 'JOG NA, NYON MONGS MNGON GYUR TZAM RE ZHIG SPANGS PA DE'I DE MA THAG TU ZAG PA THAMS CAD ZAD PA'I GROL BA THOB PAR 'GYUR RO, ZHES 'GOG PA DGONGS PA YIN NO,,
wylie: de'i phyir lam des nyan thos sde pa gnyis dang thun mong ba'i nyon mongs su bzhag pa rnams, sngar bshad pa ltar gyi lam rgyud la bskyed pas, re zhig mngon gyur du rgyu ba med pa'i tshe, nyon mongs zad pa'i grol ba thob par 'jog na, nyon mongs mngon gyur tsam re zhig spangs pa de'i de ma thag tu zag pa thams cad zad pa'i grol ba thob par 'gyur ro, zhes 'gog pa dgongs pa yin no
english: As such, the real intent of these lines is to refute the idea held by those who present the negative emotions in the same way as the two listener groups do, saying that—if we describe managing to develop within ourselves the path described earlier, and thus stopping, for the time being, the running of manifest forms of negative emotion, as attaining freedom in the form of finishing off the negative emotions—then it would be the case that just after the elimination of no more than manifest forms of negative emotion for a limited period of time, one would further reach a liberation where they had finished off each & every impurity.

acip: LAS KYI NUS PA MTHONG BA YIN, ZHES PA'I LAN DU, ,RE ZHIG NYER LEN SRED PA NI, ,MED CES NGES PA NYID CE NA, ZHES YANG SRID LEN PA'I SRED PA LAM DES ZAD PAR BYED PAS, LAS KYI DBANG GIS YANG SRID PHYI MA MI LEN PAR NGES PA NYID DO,
wylie: las kyi nus pa mthong ba yin, zhes pa'i lan du, ,re zhig nyer len sred pa ni, ,med ces nges pa nyid ce na, zhes yang srid len pa'i sred pa lam des zad par byed pas, las kyi dbang gis yang srid phyi ma mi len par nges pa nyid do
english: In response to the statement that “We can still see the forces / Of karma in them,” we find the lines, And suppose you say it's assured, Since the material cause Of initial desire is absent, For the moment. Which is to say: “Given that these paths have finished off the initial desire which causes us to take our next rebirth, it is assured that we will not be forced by karma to take this rebirth.”

acip: 'O NA DANG POR THEG CHEN DU ZHUGS PA'I DE KHO NA NYID KYI LTA BA LEGS PAR GTAN LA PHEBS PA ZHIG DANG, NYAN RANG DU LHUNG PA GNYIS GZHI MTHUN SRID PA NI DBU MA PA GNYIS KAS KYANG 'DOD DGOS LA, DE LTA NA DE 'DRA BA DES CHOS KYI BDAG MED BSGOMS PAS MNGON SUM DU 'GYUR BA DANG, DE LTAR MTHONG ZIN GOMS BAR BYED PA CIG KYANG 'DOD DGOS SO,,
wylie: 'o na dang por theg chen du zhugs pa'i de kho na nyid kyi lta ba legs par gtan la phebs pa zhig dang, nyan rang du lhung pa gnyis gzhi mthun srid pa ni dbu ma pa gnyis kas kyang 'dod dgos la, de lta na de 'dra ba des chos kyi bdag med bsgoms pas mngon sum du 'gyur ba dang, de ltar mthong zin goms bar byed pa cig kyang 'dod dgos so
english: But first of all here we can say that we need to describe, accurately, how both of the groups within the school of the Middle Way would have to agree to the concept of one person who had just entered the greater way—and succeeded in establishing, accurately, the view of suchness—who at the same time could conceivably drop into the ways of the listeners, or the self-made buddhas. And they would have to agree that, in such a circumstance, the person who had done so could have a direct experience—since they had been meditating on the lack of a self-nature to things; and they could as well undertake to accustom themselves to what they had finished seeing.

acip: LAS DE BYAS PA'I SKAD CIG GNYIS PAR ZHIG NA NI, MTSAMS DE NAS 'BRAS BU DNGOS SU 'BYIN PA'I SNGA LOGS KYI BAR DU LAS DE MED LA, LAS ZHIG PA YANG DNGOS POR MED PAS LAS LAS 'BRAS BU JI LTAR 'BYUNG BAR 'GYUR ZHES BRTZAD PA'I
wylie: las de byas pa'i skad cig gnyis par zhig na ni, mtshams de nas 'bras bu dngos su 'byin pa'i snga logs kyi bar du las de med la, las zhig pa yang dngos por med pas las las 'bras bu ji ltar 'byung bar 'gyur zhes brtsad pa'i
english: Someone might then come and make the following argument: And suppose, rather, that this karma—in the second instant of committing it—comes to a stop. From this juncture, up to the moment before the karma gives forth its consequence, the karma would not have existed. And a karma which has already stopped could never exist as a functioning thing; how then could the karma give forth its result?

acip: DE RNAMS KYI DON NI SNGAR BZHIN BRTZAD PA'I LAN SMRA BA PO BZHI GAS KYANG, LAS LA SKYE BA DANG 'GAG PA RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA KHAS LEN ZHING, LAS BYAS PA'I 'OG TU 'GAGS PA DE RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PAR 'DOD DO,,
wylie: de rnams kyi don ni sngar bzhin brtsad pa'i lan smra ba po bzhi gas kyang, las la skye ba dang 'gag pa rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa khas len zhing, las byas pa'i 'og tu 'gags pa de rang bzhin gyis grub par 'dod do
english: The import of all these points is to provide an answer to the arguments presented earlier, as all four presenters here accept the idea that karma can start & stop, by definition; and that when karma stops after we have committed it, this is something which occurs by nature.

acip: LAS 'GAGS NAS YUN RING DU LON PA LAS, 'BRAS BU 'BYUNG BA MI 'THAD PAR BRTZAD PA SON {%SO NA} GNAS PAS, SNGAR GYI LAN DE DAG GIS MI CHOG GO ZHE NA,
wylie: las 'gags nas yun ring du lon pa las, 'bras bu 'byung ba mi 'thad par brtsad pa son {%so na} gnas pas, sngar gyi lan de dag gis mi chog go zhe na
english: As such, our original argument that it would be wrong then to say that a consequence could be put forth a long time after the karma had already stopped remains a valid one. So too we can say that your replies thus far are not sufficient.

acip: DES NA RNAM SHES RIGS MTHUN CIG CAR DU SKYE BAR BRTZAD PA'I LAN DU, DE RNAMS 'JUG PA MYUR BAS RIM GYIS SKYE YANG CIG CAR DU SKYE BAR MNGON ZHES 'CHAD DGOS PA 'DRA BA ZHIG SNANG YANG
wylie: des na rnam shes rigs mthun cig car du skye bar brtsad pa'i lan du, de rnams 'jug pa myur bas rim gyis skye yang cig car du skye bar mngon zhes 'chad dgos pa 'dra ba zhig snang yang
english: As such, it would appear that such people have to give the following response to the challenge of asking how it is that specific sustained flows of awareness can arise. That is, they would have to make explanations like saying that the way these awarenesses engage is very quick, and so—even though they are arising one after the other—it appears as though they are coming up all together.

acip: BDAG DANG MA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD KYIS THOG MA MED PA NAS DA LTA'I BAR DU, SPYIR 'KHOR BA DANG KHYAD PAR NGAN SONG GSUM GYI SDUG BSNGAL SNA TSOGS ZHIG MYONG 'DUG TU ZIN KYANG, DA DUNG SDUG BSNGAL GYI GTING DANG MTHA' MNGON PAR DKA' BAR 'DUG ,
wylie: bdag dang ma sems can thams cad kyis thog ma med pa nas da lta'i bar du, spyir 'khor ba dang khyad par ngan song gsum gyi sdug bsngal sna tshogs zhig myong 'dug tu zin kyang, da dung sdug bsngal gyi gting dang mtha' mngon par dka' bar 'dug
english: "For time with no beginning, and up to the present moment, I and every living being there is--each one my mother--have had to go through all the myriad pains of the cycle of suffering in general, and more specifically the miseries of the three lower realms.  That much is finished; and yet the depths and reaches of the pain still to come to us is something that can hardly be imagined.

acip: GANG LA SBYIN NA SLOB MA LA NI'O, ,SLOB MA CI 'DRA BA ZHIG SNYAM NA, KHYAD PAR GNYIS DANG LDAN PA STE DANG PO NI, SANGS RGYAS DANG CHOS DANG DGE 'DUN TE DKON MCHOG GSUM LA SKYABS SU SONG BA STE SKYABS 'GRO THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I SDOM PA DANG LDAN PA'O, ,GNYIS PA NI, BSAM PA DAG PA STE SMON PA DANG 'JUG PA'I BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS RNAM PA GNYIS TSUL BZHIN DU BSKYED PA'O, ,'DIS NI SNGAGS DANG PHAR PHYIN GYI THEG PA GNYIS KYI THUN MONG BA'I LAM GYI RIM PAR LA BLO LEGS PAR SBYANGS PA LA GZHUNG 'DI 'CHANG PAR BSTAN NO,
wylie: gang la sbyin na slob ma la ni'o, ,slob ma ci 'dra ba zhig snyam na, khyad par gnyis dang ldan pa ste dang po ni, sangs rgyas dang chos dang dge 'dun te dkon mchog gsum la skyabs su song ba ste skyabs 'gro thun mong ma yin pa'i sdom pa dang ldan pa'o, ,gnyis pa ni, bsam pa dag pa ste smon pa dang 'jug pa'i byang chub kyi sems rnam pa gnyis tshul bzhin du bskyed pa'o, ,'dis ni sngags dang phar phyin gyi theg pa gnyis kyi thun mong ba'i lam gyi rim par la blo legs par sbyangs pa la gzhung 'di 'chang par bstan no
english: Who is it that we should grant this teaching on how to behave towards our Lama?  It should be granted to a worthy disciple.  And what is it that makes them worthy?  The disciple should be possessed of two characteristics. First of all, they must be someone who has already gone for shelter to the Three Jewels: to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Community.  That is to say, they must be possessed of the unique vow of refuge. The disciple must secondly be "one of a pure heart," which means that they must have given birth, in the proper way, to both forms of the Wish for enlightenment: the Wish as a prayer, and the Wish in action. The point here that the root text of the Fifty Verses is making is that a potential disciple for its teaching must be one whose mind has been perfectly prepared, by using the steps of the path which are shared by both the way of the secret word and the way of the perfections. ***

acip: DE LA YUL LNGA BSTEN PAS NYON MONGS SKYE LA, DE YANG NGAN 'GRO'I RGYUR 'GYUR ZHES BRTZAD PA LA, YUL BSTEN PA LAS SKYES PA'I NYON MONGS LA NYAN THOS LA SOGS PA DE KHO NA NYID MA RTOGS PA LA NGAN 'GRO'I RGYU DANG, RTOGS PA LA SANGS RGYAS KYI RGYUR 'GYUR BA GNYIS SU PHYE BA'I LAN MDZAD KYI, 'DOD YON BSTEN PA LAS NYON MONGS MI SKYED CES MA GSUNGS SO,,
wylie: de la yul lnga bsten pas nyon mongs skye la, de yang ngan 'gro'i rgyur 'gyur zhes brtsad pa la, yul bsten pa las skyes pa'i nyon mongs la nyan thos la sogs pa de kho na nyid ma rtogs pa la ngan 'gro'i rgyu dang, rtogs pa la sangs rgyas kyi rgyur 'gyur ba gnyis su phye ba'i lan mdzad kyi, 'dod yon bsten pa las nyon mongs mi skyed ces ma gsungs so
english: Someone might react to this by arguing that using the five objects of the senses leads to a mental affliction, and that this then acts as a cause that leads us to the births of misery.  The way you have to phrase the answer to this argument is by splitting your reply; you need to say, "When you do use these objects, it gives rise to mental afflictions.  For those like practitioners on the listener track who have yet to perceive suchness, these mental afflictions act as a cause for the lower births.  For those who have perceived suchness, these same afflictions act as a cause for enlightenment."  You shouldn't try to respond to this argument by saying that using these objects doesn't give rise to mental afflictions.
